To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a regression model is proposed to estimate K(d) values of heavy metals in risk assessment studies and that this approach is applied to lead, allowing a considerable improvement of the estimation uncertainty.

a) a regression equation to predict the partition coefficient of Pb in water-soil systems was developed, b) the equation was validated using independent data and c) the equation was applied to predict K(d) values of Pb in soils of the Po Plain.

a) A regression model to estimate the K(d) values for heavy metals was proposed and applied to lead; b) A pH-dependent regression equation for the soil-water distribution of lead was obtained: log K(d) = 1.99 + 0.42 pH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a regression model for K(d) of Pb in soils, and its application to the risk assessment of contaminated soils.
the development of regression models to predict K(d) for a number of metals (Pb, Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Zn).
the development of a rapid and simple method to estimate K(d) values of Pb and other heavy metals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed equation is a valid alternative to the use of the conservative K(d) value for Pb in the risk assessment of heavy metals.
the K(d) of heavy metals in soils is a function of the pH and the ionic strength of the soil solution, the latter depending on the soil moisture and the soil texture.
the proposed model provides a good estimation of K(d) for Pb in soils, with an average error of 0.3 orders of magnitude, which is a considerable improvement with respect to the conventional approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple and rapid regression model can be applied for a preliminary screening of the heavy metals mobility, allowing a considerable improvement of the risk assessment process.
a regression equation for the estimation of the K(d) of heavy metals is proposed for Pb, which is pH dependent.
the proposed equation allows a fast, accurate, and reliable estimation of K(d) for Pb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple model can be applied at a screening level to reduce the uncertainty in the estimation of K(d) values, thus reducing the uncertainty in the risk assessment process.
the pH-dependent K(d) value is a better predictor of the mobility of heavy metals in soils than the pH-independent K(d) value.
the proposed model is able to predict the soil-water distribution of Pb with a reasonable uncertainty, and that the model could be applied to other heavy metals as well.
